items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: I was spiked playing Little League baseball when I was eight years old, and it developed into osteomyelitis, which is what Mickey Mantle had.

ctx.x: I think he was with the group that — we saw them not that long ago.

Yes. He’s been with the band off and on all these years. Yeah. He has great stamina to play and travel like that. I really commend his endurance. But we had a wonderful time. What I can say, John Clayton was very elegant with his approach you know, to playing in the rhythm section. And when Cleveland Eaton came, he put a real greasy groove which was necessary to the Basie sound, and that gave us a certain spark and a certain element of the groove that Basie loved so much. And it became a new era in the band. And…
Sometimes the younger musicians that, well like myself, I always wanted to do a big band, but I never saw the downside of it perhaps — that night after night.
